priceSnapshot.source: OKX public API v5 /market/ticker BTC-USDT, keyless, fetched via the run's web_fetch proxy. Response ts 1786172824264 = 2026-08-08T07:07:04Z = 02:07:04 COT, three seconds behind the wall clock at fetch time, so this is a live tick and not a cached one. changePct is measured against the COMPLETED 07 Aug UTC daily close of 64,916.5: (65,006.0 - 64,916.5) / 64,916.5 = +0.138%, rounded to +0.14%.
priceSnapshot.note: BTC made a quiet but real advance overnight. Spot is 65,006.0, which is 129.1 points above the 64,876.9 the endday session stamped at 19:47 COT Friday, +0.20% over six hours and twenty minutes. More important than the size of the move is where it happened: the 07 Aug UTC daily bar CLOSED at 64,916.5 and the 08 Aug bar has traded 64,821.8 to 65,073.5 so far, so price spent the whole Friday-night gap ABOVE the 64,650 reduce line the desk has now published for four consecutive sessions, and it never came within 200 points of it. The lowest 1H CLOSE since the endday stamp is 64,878.6 and the lowest TRADE is 64,869.0 in the 00:45Z fifteen-minute bar - 219 points of clearance. Volume behaved exactly as a Friday-night tape should: the 00:00Z hour turned over 91.79 BTC as the New York close washed through, then decayed to 42.88 BTC in the 06:00Z hour and 1.25 BTC in the in-progress 07:00Z bar. 24h volume is 3,264.68 BTC against a 24h range of 64,303.1 to 65,388.0. The single thing that changed the character of the tape is the 03:00Z-to-05:00Z stretch, where price stepped from 64,921.1 up through 65,036.0 and 65,006.9 on 83.9 and 56.4 BTC - modest size, but it took out the 64,975-65,020 shelf that had capped every attempt since 22:00Z and it has held above it since.

reduceIf.confirmation: A 1H CLOSE below $64,650 - held UNCHANGED for a FOURTH consecutive session, and the level has now gone a full overnight without being tested at all. The morning session published it, the midday held it against a low that traded 130.8 points through it, the endday held it again, and across the six hours since the endday stamp the lowest hourly close is 64,878.6 with the lowest trade at 64,869.0. What sits there has changed slightly in the desk's favour: the daily EMA50 has risen to 64,696.29 and the 1H EMA50 to 64,721.42, so the moving-average cluster is now ABOVE the trigger rather than sitting on it, which means a 1H close under 64,650 would already be a close beneath both. Below the line the CoinGlass heatmap reads 1.09M of leveraged exposure at 64,515.85 and 1.22M at 64,446.74. Spot is 65,006, so the line is 356 points below, 0.55%, well inside a 2.23% daily ATR.

addIf.confirmation: A 1H CLOSE above $65,120 - a deliberate STEP DOWN from the endday's 4H-close-above-65,400, which asked for more than the tape can plausibly deliver on a weekend and which is 383 points ABOVE the magnet price is actually being pulled toward. 65,120 sits just over the 65,073.5 session high and just under the 65,137.84 shelf, where the heatmap shows only 191.00K of exposure - the thinnest reading anywhere between spot and 65,900. Clearing it on an hourly close opens a 363-point run into the 65,483.39 cluster, which at 1.58M is the single brightest band on the entire 48-hour map and sits within a rounding error of the 1.59M scale maximum. This is the trigger that matters this session, not the reduce.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from the endday's REDUCE to ADD. Three things justify the flip and none of them is price alone. FIRST, the moving-average picture completed overnight: 4H, 1H and 15m all now have price above EMA20, EMA50, EMA100 and EMA200 simultaneously - twelve of twelve - and the daily has reclaimed its EMA50 at 64,696.29 with the histogram positive at +19.95. SECOND, the ETF read the endday had to publish as provisional resolved upward: IBIT's 07 Aug row landed at +86.7M and the day's total went from a printed +15.0M to a final +101.7M, turning a decelerating streak into a genuine five-day, +865.3M sequence. THIRD, and most concrete, the liquidity map inverted in the desk's favour - the biggest magnet on the board is now ABOVE spot at 65,483.39 and 0.73% away, while directly beneath price there is an air pocket from roughly 64,650 to 64,930 with a literal zero reading. The stop order stays OFF: the wallet's exposure is spot-only and spot cannot carry a resting stop, and the gap to the morning session is only about four and a half hours.

liquidation.note: The defining feature of this map. 1.58M of leveraged exposure against a colour-scale maximum of 1.59M - this is the brightest band anywhere in the 48-hour window, and it is 477 points above spot, 0.73%, roughly a third of a daily ATR. It has been building all through the Friday session and it did not discharge on the 65,388 spike, which means the exposure is still resting there. Everything between spot and this level is thin: 191.00K at 65,137.84 and 300.88K at 65,345.17 are the only readings in between, so once 65,120 goes on an hourly close there is very little in the way.

768.74K, the second-heaviest band above spot. It sits 207 points beyond the 65,483.39 magnet, which matters because it means a squeeze that clears 65,483 does not immediately run into empty air - there is a second shelf to absorb it. Together the two bands hold 2.35M between 65,483 and 65,691, and that pair is the realistic ceiling for any weekend push.

300.88K. A minor waystation, not a barrier. Notable mainly because it is the last reading before the 65,483.39 cluster and because it sits 55 points under the 65,400 level the endday session was using as its add trigger - which is a fair illustration of why that trigger was in the wrong place.
274.09K. Beyond the realistic reach of a thin weekend session, listed so the upside ladder is complete. Above it the map thins sharply: 176.71K at 66,381.82 and 284.25K at 67,349.36.

191.00K, the LIGHTEST band between spot and 65,900, sitting 64 points above the 65,073.5 session high. This is exactly the kind of level that offers no resistance once an hourly bar closes through it, which is why the add trigger was placed at 65,120 rather than higher.

ZERO. Not a typo - the heatmap reads a literal 0 here, and the same 0 repeats at 64,792.29, 64,723.18 and 64,654.07. There is an AIR POCKET of roughly 280 points directly beneath spot with no resting leveraged exposure whatsoever. It cuts both ways and both ways matter: nothing there will attract price downward, but equally nothing there will absorb a sell order. If 64,930 breaks in weekend liquidity the first thing waiting is 64,515.85, 415 points lower.

1.09M, and the nearest meaningful band below spot at 490 points, 0.75%. This is where a weekend air-pocket slide would find its first real bid. It sits 20 points under the 4H EMA20 at 64,535.71, so a move that reaches it has already broken the shortest moving average of the bullish stack.

1.22M, the heaviest band below spot and only 69 points beneath the 64,515.85 shelf. The pair holds 2.31M between 64,447 and 64,516, which is the downside mirror of the 65,483/65,691 pair above - roughly matched in size but 63 points further away from spot on a percentage basis.
718.27K. A third downside shelf, 1,043 points under spot. Reaching it would take a move of 1.60%, which is inside a single daily ATR but would require the 64,447 pair to fail first.
503.57K, wedged between the 64,447 pair and the 63,963 shelf. It is 23 points above the 1H EMA200 at 64,285.63.
530.48K. Deep downside, listed for completeness. Below it the map is essentially empty until 63,064.54 at 161.79K.
284.25K, far above spot and above the daily EMA100 at 67,059.49. Included because it is the last band of any size on the upside within the plotted window.
161.79K, the floor of the plotted window. Not reachable in a single session at current volatility.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is UP and the asymmetry is not close. Above spot: 1.58M at 65,483.39, 477 points and 0.73% away, the brightest band on the whole map. Below spot: 1.09M at 64,515.85, 490 points and 0.75% away. The upside cluster is both nearer and 45% heavier. Sharpening it further, the path up is nearly clear - only 191.00K at 65,137.84 and 300.88K at 65,345.17 stand in the way - while the path down starts with a 280-point stretch of literal zero from about 64,930 to 64,650. That zero is the honest caveat on an otherwise bullish reading: an empty pocket is not support, it is simply the absence of a magnet, and in a Saturday book a single sizeable market sell could travel through it very quickly before finding the 64,516 bid.

atr.source: Wilder ATR(14) computed on the OKX bar=1Dutc series, stated on the LAST COMPLETED daily bar (07 Aug UTC, high 65,388.0, low 64,159.6, prior close 64,325.8, TR = 1,228.4). timeframes.structure: Split, and the split is the whole macro story. Price at 65,006 is ABOVE the EMA20 at 64,177.20 and above the EMA50 at 64,696.29 - the second consecutive session holding that reclaim - but it is 3.1% BELOW the EMA100 at 67,059.49 and 11.3% below the EMA200 at 73,287.66. The EMA50 sitting above the EMA20 is a bear cross that has not repaired. So the correct framing is a recovery inside a downtrend, not a trend change: everything constructive on the 4H and 1H is happening beneath a daily structure that still has to climb 2,053 points to reach its own EMA100. MACD is the encouraging half - the line crossed above signal and the histogram at +19.95 is the third consecutive positive print, having gone from roughly +22 to +66 to +19.95 as the 07 Aug bar closed. calibration.rollingRecord: 54 rows on file before this one. The endday session called range with a bullish tilt at 34/46/20 from 64,876.9, set position to REDUCE, held reduce at 64,650 and add at a 4H close above 65,400. Price is 65,006.0. The DIRECTION was right - the tilt was bullish and price rose 129.1 points, +0.20% - but the STANCE was defensive against that direction, so the two disagreed with each other. Neither trigger fired: the lowest 1H close was 64,878.6 against a 64,650 reduce, and the session high of 65,073.5 fell 326.5 points short of the 65,400 add. That is the second consecutive session in which the add trigger was placed beyond anything the tape could reach, which is why this run steps it down to 65,120.
calibration.note: The endday row backfills to price_next_report 65,006.0, reduce_fired false, add_fired false, acting_helped FALSE. The false is deliberate and slightly harsh on a good piece of reasoning: the endday's REDUCE was an explicit risk-shape decision rather than a directional call - it sold 15% of an all-in spot book to avoid carrying naked exposure through an unprotected Friday-night gap - and it said so plainly at the time. The gap turned out benign, price rose, and the trim therefore cost roughly 0.2% on the fifteen percent it sold, about four cents of equity. Scored on outcome it did not help. Scored on process it was defensible, and the cash it raised is precisely what this session is now able to deploy at a better-confirmed moment. Both things are true and the calibration file records the outcome, not the intent.
